<path>/private/tmp/hima-l4-cARyBM/hima-home-RbqF8A/profiles/hima/node_modules/@hima/harness/skills/knowledge/pack-anatomy.md</path>
<type>file</type>
<content>
1: # What a pack folder holds, file by file
2: 
3: The skeleton the fabric stage compiles to. Every block below is the **smallest file of its kind that
4: this harness accepts**, with one note per field saying what that field is for. Nothing here is a
5: method: the ids, the paths, the units and the numbers are stand-ins, and what they should be for the
6: pack you are writing is the spec's to say and never this file's.
7: 
8: Read this for shape. Read the pack installed beside the folder you are authoring for a whole example
9: of the first two, written by hand for a real business. Ask `hima_pack_check` whether what you wrote
10: is a pack: it names every fault in the pack's own files, and that answer is the authority no
11: skeleton can be.
12: 
13: A pack folder holds, at its top: `contract.yml`, `graph.yml`, `semantics.yml` where the pack's own
14: readers emit value types, and the directories `rules/`, `choosers/`, `readers/`, `knowledge/` and
15: `tools/` where it has files for them. Every path in it is a plain file with a plain name — no link,
16: no hidden name, nothing but letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores in each segment.
17: 
18: ## `contract.yml` — what a Site must bind, what a generation produces, what the pack runs
19: 
20: ```yaml
21: id: example-probe            # the folder's own name; lowercase letters, digits and dashes
22: version: '1'                 # a string, and graph.yml states the same one
23: title: Example probe         # what a person reads the pack under
24: 
25: inputs:                      # what a Site binds in its own site file; the pack binds none of them
26:   - name: flowRoot
27:     description: The Golden Flow's root on the Site. Read where it lies, never written.
28:   - name: design
29:     description: What the flow is run over, spelled as the flow's own manifests spell it.
30:   - name: workspaceRoot
31:     description: Where campaign workspaces are made; the Site's permit must allow writes under it.
32: 
33: outputs:                     # what a generation leaves in its own workspace
34:   - name: measurement
35:     path: flow/out/${design}/measurement.txt   # relative to the workspace; ${…} is an input above
36:     reader: measurement-file                    # the reader that turns it into typed values
37:     description: What this generation measured. The judged file.
38:   - name: toolLog
39:     path: flow/logs/${design}/tool.log         # no reader: a file a person reads after a failure
40:     description: What the tool said while it ran.
41: 
42: environment:
43:   wrappers:                  # the first word of every command line below — a tool's argv[0] and a
44:     - make                   #   reader's; the Site's permit decides each, and a word not here is
45:     - sh                     #   refused before a campaign starts
46: 
47: workspace:
48:   copy:                      # what is copied out of flowRoot into <workspace>/flow/, once per campaign
49:     - Makefile
50:     - tools
51:     - inputs/${design}
52: 
53: tools:
54:   - id: measure
55:     file: tools/measure.sh   # the script a person can run by hand, under this folder's tools/
56:     description: One generation of the flow's own measuring stage, in the campaign's copy of it.
57:     inputs: [WORKSPACE, DESIGN, STEP_MS]   # the variables the script reads, and the only names argv may use
58:     licences:                # optional: what a job of this tool holds on the Site while it runs
59:       measuring-seat: 1      # the Site declares how many it has; a tool that holds none writes no block
60:     argv:                    # what the harness launches; argv[0] is the wrapper above
61:       - make
62:       - -C
63:       - ${WORKSPACE}/flow
64:       - DESIGN=${DESIGN}
65:       - measure
66:       - STEP_MS=${STEP_MS}
67: 
68: rules:                       # the judge rules this pack may apply, by id: this folder's rules/ first,
69:   - measurement-within-bound #   the bundle's second
70: 
71: knowledge:                   # optional: this pack's own domain knowledge, one entry per file
72:   - file: the-step-method.md
73:     purpose: why this pack changes the step the way it does
74: 
75: strategy:                    # what a run is set to for one generation; at least one knob, each whole
76:   stepMs: { type: number, unit: ms, min: 0.5, max: 10, default: 2 }
77:   shape: { type: choice, options: [plain, dense], default: plain }
78: 
79: words:                       # what a person reads each number under: one entry per goal parameter the
80:   measurement_at_most: { label: measurement at most, unit: ms }   # graph binds, one per knob above
81:   stepMs: { label: step, unit: ms }
82:   shape: { label: shape }    # a choice states no unit: a choice is measured in nothing
83: ```
84: 
85: ## Workshop declaration and graph binding
86: 
87: A Workshop is an existing `act` node variant. Its input reports are contract `outputs` produced by
88: earlier nodes; scalar `inputs` are bound by the node. Knowledge files also appear in the contract's
89: `knowledge`. The following is an additional block within `contract.yml`, not a separate file:
90: 
91: ```yaml
92: outputs:
93:   - name: measuredInput
94:     path: flow/out/${design}/measurement.txt
95:     reader: measurement-file
96:     description: The preceding tool's measurement.
97:   - name: analysis
98:     path: research/analysis/result.txt
99:     reader: measurement-file
100:     description: The script's derived measurement, checked by the reader and Judge.
101: environment:
102:   wrappers: [sh]
103: knowledge:
104:   - file: analysis-method.md
105:     purpose: How the measurements support the analysis.
106: workshops:
107:   - id: analyze
108:     purpose: Read measuredInput and write a script deriving the requested measurement from its actual data.
109:     directory: research/analysis
110:     entry: entry.sh
111:     language: sh
112:     inputs: [LIMIT]
113:     reads: [measuredInput]
114:     knowledge: [analysis-method.md]
115:     produces: analysis
116:     argv: [sh, '${ENTRY}', '${WORKSHOP}', '${LIMIT}']
117:     licences: {}             # omit when no licensed resource is needed
118: ```
119: 
120: The corresponding graph node and downstream read are real nodes, connected after the input producer:
121: 
122: ```yaml
123: - id: analyze
124:   kind: act
125:   parameters:
126:     workshop: analyze
127:     arguments:
128:       LIMIT: { from: strategy, name: stepMs }
129: - id: read-analysis
130:   kind: act
131:   parameters:
132:     observes: analysis
133: ```
134: 
135: `reads` are output names, not arbitrary paths. `produces` is an output name, not a value type.
136: The output's reader emits types declared by `semantics.yml`; downstream Judge rules consume those
137: types. `directory` is relative to the Campaign workspace and cannot be `flow` or the readers'
138: reserved directory. `entry` is one filename. `argv[0]` is a declared Site wrapper, and `argv[1]`
139: is exactly `${ENTRY}`. A script may produce a declared output elsewhere in the Campaign workspace;
140: its code-writing tool is confined to `directory`. Neither may escape the Site permit.
141: 
142: The script is called as `sh entry.sh <workshop> <limit>`, so shell `$1` is the workshop and `$2`
143: is the limit. Reader scripts have their own argv: in the reader example below `$1` is `${REPORT}`
144: and `$2` is `${OUT}`. These are argv arrays; do not put a shell command, pipe or redirection in them.
145: 
146: ## `graph.yml` — the four node kinds, the outcomes the edges are taken on, and the one edge back
147: 
148: ```yaml
149: id: example-probe            # the contract's id
150: version: '1'                 # the contract's version
151: entry: measure               # the node a campaign starts at
152: 
153: nodes:
154:   - id: measure              # act: run one of the contract's tools on the Site and wait for it
155:     kind: act
156:     parameters:
157:       tool: measure
158:       arguments:             # what the Run supplies for this generation
159:         STEP_MS: { from: strategy, name: stepMs }
160: 
161:   - id: read-measurement     # act: read one of the contract's outputs into the ledger
162:     kind: act
163:     parameters:
164:       observes: measurement
165: 
166:   - id: judge                # judge: apply rules in order; the edge out is chosen by the first one's outcome
167:     kind: judge
168:     parameters:
169:       rules: [measurement-within-bound]
170:       bind:                  # what binds each parameter a rule declares
171:         bound_ms: { from: goal, name: measurement_at_most }
172: 
173:   - id: next-step            # explore: choose the next strategy, or open a loop of its own
174:     kind: explore
175:     parameters:
176:       chooser: step-back-off # by id, exactly as a rule is named
177:       bind:                  # the numbers the chooser leaves to the pack author
178:         marginMs: 0.05
179:       converge:              # optional, and all four together: when this loop has stopped learning
180:         read: measured       # one of the chooser's own `reads`
181:         band: 0.05           # how far apart two generations must be to count as movement
182:         generations: 1       # how many successive generations must have moved by less than that
183:         generationLimit: 6   # what this pack thinks a campaign of it should be allowed at most
184: 
185:   - id: blocked              # wait: where a run stops for a person once its retries are spent
186:     kind: wait
187:     parameters:
188:       blocker: hard-blocker
189: 
190: edges:
191:   - { from: measure, to: read-measurement }            # an act node's one unlabelled edge out
192:   - { from: read-measurement, to: judge }
193:   - { from: judge, to: next-step, outcome: PASS }      # a judge node's edges carry their outcome
194:   - { from: judge, to: next-step, outcome: FAIL }
195:   - { from: next-step, to: measure, revisit: true }    # the loop: the only edge that goes back
196: ```
197: 
198: ## `semantics.yml` — what the value types this pack's own readers emit mean
199: 
200: Written **only** where this pack's own readers emit a value type. A pack whose outputs are all read
201: by readers the harness ships declares none and writes no such file.
202: 
203: The two qualifier vocabularies are the harness's own and are **fixed**: `mode` is `setup` or `hold`,
204: `scope` is `all` or `reg2reg`. Declaring either means every reading of that type carries one of the
205: listed words; declaring neither means a reading of it carries no qualifier at all.
206: 
207: ```yaml
208: values:
209:   measured_ms:               # the slug a reader emits and a rule or chooser reads
210:     unit: ms                 # what a value of it is measured in; every reading is held to this
211:     mode: [setup, hold]      # optional: the analysis passes a value of it can belong to
212:     scope: [all, reg2reg]    # optional: the path groups a value of it can cover
213:     description: what this generation measured, as the file states it
214: ```
215: 
216: ## `rules/<id>.yml` — one judge rule
217: 
218: ```yaml
219: id: measurement-within-bound # the file's own name, without the .yml
220: version: '1'
221: title: The measurement is within the bound the run was started with
222: parameter:                   # optional: the one value a node binds at judge time
223:   name: bound_ms
224:   unit: ms
225: requires:                    # what must have been observed for this rule to have an opinion at all
226:   - type: measured_ms
227: subject:                     # the value the predicate is about
228:   type: measured_ms
229: predicate:
230:   op: lte                    # lte, gte and the like
231:   threshold: { parameter: bound_ms }   # or a number written here
232:   unit: ms
233: ```
234: 
235: ## `choosers/<id>.yml` — one explore move, as data
236: 
237: ```yaml
238: id: step-back-off
239: version: '1'
240: title: Take the step back by what the last generation missed by
241: parameter:                   # the one number the pack binds in its explore node's `bind:`
242:   name: marginMs
243:   unit: ms
244: reads:                       # what is read out of the run's latest observation, by type
245:   measured: { type: measured_ms, unit: ms }
246: decide:                      # first matching clause wins
247:   - when: { constraint: PASS, goal: PASS }
248:     goalMet: true            # the goal is reached; there is no next strategy
249:   - when: { constraint: PASS }
250:     next:                    # sets this pack's own strategy knobs by name; a knob not named carries over
251:       stepMs: { sum: [measured, marginMs] }
252:   - when: { constraint: FAIL }
253:     next:
254:       stepMs: { sum: [measured, { neg: marginMs }] }
255: ```
256: 
257: ## `readers/<id>.yml` and its script under `tools/` — a reader of this pack's own
258: 
259: ```yaml
260: id: measurement-file
261: version: '1'
262: file: tools/read-measurement.sh   # under this folder's tools/, and a plain file
263: argv:                             # every word is a literal, or exactly one of the four placeholders
264:   - sh                            # argv[0] is the wrapper: a literal word the contract declares
265:   - ${READER}                     # the script's path on the Site
266:   - ${REPORT}                     # the output the contract pointed it at
267:   - ${OUT}                        # the file the script must write
268: reportKind: example-measurement   # a word for the record; never sniffed
269: emits: [measured_ms]              # every value type it writes, each declared in the semantics
270: ```
271: 
272: Its script, under this folder's `tools/`, launched by the harness as a job under the Site's permit
273: with the report and the output file as arguments:
274: 
275: ```sh
276: #!/bin/sh
277: # tools/read-measurement.sh — reads $1 (the report) and writes the reading document to $2.
278: set -eu
279: printf '{"values":[{"type":"measured_ms","unit":"ms","mode":"setup","scope":"all","value":%s}]}\n' \
280:   "$(awk '/^measured/ { print $2 }' "$1")" > "$2"
281: ```
282: 
283: What it writes to `${OUT}` — one JSON document, and exit 0:
284: 
285: ```json
286: { "values": [ { "type": "measured_ms", "unit": "ms", "mode": "setup", "scope": "all", "value": 2.5 } ] }
287: ```
288: 
289: A value carries `mode` and `scope` exactly when the semantics above declare them for its type, and
290: the word it carries is one of the declared ones. It may also carry `group` (the tool's own name for
291: the path group the number came from) and, where the report did not state the number at all,
292: `"value": null` with `unknownReason` saying why — never a zero standing in for a number nobody read.
293: A value whose type, unit or qualifiers are not the declared ones is refused, and the reading never
294: becomes an observation.
295: 
296: ## `knowledge/<file>.md` — one piece of this pack's domain knowledge
297: 
298: A plain Markdown file, one per entry of the contract's `knowledge:`, written for the purpose that
299: entry gives it. Nothing reads it as data; it is what a model moment of this pack is given.
300: 
301: ```markdown
302: # Why this pack changes the step the way it does
303: 
304: <the reasoning, in the author's own words, for the purpose the contract declares>
305: ```
306: 
307: ## The five records the pipeline writes
308: 
309: Each is written by one stage, and each is what carries the folder one rung further up. They are the
310: authoring account and not the pack — no campaign reads one — and the digest of the files a campaign
311: runs is taken without them.
312: 
313: | File | Written by | Sections, in this order |
314: | --- | --- | --- |
315: | `INTENT.md` | `/hima-grill` | `Business`, `Golden Flow`, `Answers`, `Ambiguities resolved`, `Knowledge applied` |
316: | `SPEC.md` | `/hima-spec` | `Goal template`, `Constraints`, `Run contract`, `Semantics`, `Judge rules`, `Choosers`, `Endings`, `Workshops`, `Knowledge` |
317: | `FABRIC.md` | `/hima-fabric` | `Files written`, `Gaps`, `Reviews` |
318: | `TEST.md` | `/hima-test` | `Site`, `Run`, `Ending`, `Generations`, `Code`, `Refusals`, `Disagreements` |
319: | `VERSION.yml` | `/hima-release`, through the harness's own verb | `pack`, `version`, `released`, `test: { record, run }`, `files:` — one sha256 per file |
320: 
321: A record validates when its ordered `##` headings are **exactly** those sections: nothing missing,
322: nothing extra, nothing twice, nothing out of order, nothing empty. `VERSION.yml` is the one of the
323: five nobody writes by hand: every hash in it is computed by the harness over the bytes in the folder.

1: # The run contract of the opene902 timing probe: what a Site must bind before this pack can run,
2: # what a generation produces inside the Campaign workspace, and what the pack runs on the Site.
3: # `/hima pack check <pack> --site <site>` reads this file against a Site's own and reports every
4: # input that is not bound, every wrapper the Permit will not run, and every rule or reader that does
5: # not exist.
6: id: opene902-timing-probe
7: version: '2'
8: title: opene902 timing probe
9: 
10: # What a Site binds, in its site file under `bindings:`. The same pack runs on another Site by
11: # editing that file, never this one.
12: inputs:
13:   - name: flowRoot
14:     description: >-
15:       The Golden Flow's root on the Site: the directory holding the makefile the flow is driven by.
16:       Read-only to a Campaign — a generation runs in its own copy of it, never here.
17:   - name: design
18:     description: The design the flow builds, spelled as the flow's own manifests spell it.
19:   - name: workspaceRoot
20:     description: >-
21:       Where Campaign workspaces are created. The Site's Permit must allow writes under it; nothing
22:       the pack does writes anywhere else.
23: 
24: # What a generation leaves in its Campaign workspace. Paths are relative to the workspace, with

33:     description: What dc_shell said while it ran. Read by a person after a failure, not by a reader.

36: # `allowedWrappers` decides each one, so a pack cannot introduce a command a Site owner never allowed.

38:   wrappers:

41: # How a Campaign workspace is prepared from the bound flow root, once per Campaign. The copy lands in
42: # `<workspace>/flow/`, which is the pack anatomy's fixed place for it (see README, "Pack anatomy").
43: workspace:
44:   copy:
45:     - Makefile

60:       `FORCE_SYNTH=1` so no generation ever reuses another's netlist, and `EDA_CONTAINER_NAME` so the

64:     # What a Job of this tool holds on the Site for as long as it runs: one Design Compiler seat.
65:     # The Site declares how many it has under `capacity.licences`, and the count is held across every

1: # The opene902 timing probe as a HimaFabric graph, and the Loop it explores in: synthesize at the
2: # strategy's clock period, read what it produced, judge it, choose the next strategy — and go round
3: # again with that strategy, generation after generation, until the goal is met, the periods stop
4: # moving, or the campaign's generation limit is spent.
5: #
6: # Four node kinds and no more (CONTEXT.md): act, judge, explore, wait. An act node has one unlabelled
7: # edge out; a judge node's edges carry the outcome they are taken on. A node with no outgoing edge
8: # ends the Run.
9: #
10: # The loop is the last edge below, `next-period` back to `synthesize`, marked `revisit: true` (D43).
11: # Following it is what opens the next generation, with the period the explore node just chose. It is
12: # the only edge in this graph that goes backwards, and the only kind of edge allowed to: a loop a
13: # reader cannot see in this file is a loop the engine would be running behind it.
14: id: opene902-timing-probe
15: version: '2'
16: entry: synthesize
17: 
18: nodes:
19:   # Act: run the pack's tool on the Site, in the Campaign workspace, and wait for it.
20:   - id: synthesize
21:     kind: act
22:     parameters:
23:       tool: synth
24:       # Only the strategy knob is chosen per generation. WORKSPACE, FLOW_ROOT, DESIGN and CAMPAIGN
25:       # are the Run's own workspace and the Site's bindings, which the fabric already holds — and
26:       # which a node may not bind: a pack that named one here would not load.
27:       arguments:
28:         PERIOD_NS: { from: strategy, name: periodNs }
29: 
30:   # Act: read the report that generation produced into HimaLedger, through the contract's own reader.
31:   - id: read-qor
32:     kind: act
33:     parameters:
34:       observes: qorReport
35: 
36:   # Judge: the setup rule first, then the goal rule whose target the Run's goal binds. The outgoing
37:   # edge is chosen by the outcome of the first rule listed.
38:   - id: judge
39:     kind: judge
40:     parameters:
41:       rules:
42:         - setup-wns-all-nonnegative
43:         - clock-period-at-most
44:       bind:
45:         target_period_ns: { from: goal, name: target_period_ns }
46: 
47:   # Method version 2: a met constraint is tested one step tighter; a violation proposes
48:   # period + |slack| - stepNs. This candidate is a hypothesis, not a measured closed period.
49:   # Convergence means the observed periods stopped moving, even if setup still fails.
50:   # Only a generation passing both setup and goal can end goal-met.
51:   # generationLimit is a budget bound, not a claim that the goal is reachable.
52:   - id: next-period
53:     kind: explore
54:     parameters:
55:       chooser: over-constraining-push
56:       bind:
57:         stepNs: 0.05
58:       converge:
59:         read: period
60:         band: 0.05
61:         generations: 1
62:         generationLimit: 6
63: 
64:   # Wait: where a Run stops for a person once its Retry allowance is spent. Nothing draws an edge
65:   # here, and nothing needs to: a Hard blocker is routed to the graph's wait node by the fabric
66:   # itself, exactly as an UNDETERMINED the pack labelled no edge for is. A pack declares where its
67:   # Runs wait; it does not have to draw an edge from every node that might fail.
68:   - id: blocked
69:     kind: wait
70:     parameters:
71:       blocker: hard-blocker
72: 
73: edges:
74:   - { from: synthesize, to: read-qor }
75:   - { from: read-qor, to: judge }
76:   - { from: judge, to: next-period, outcome: PASS }
77:   - { from: judge, to: next-period, outcome: FAIL }
78:   # The loop: taken only when the decision chose a next strategy. A decision of goal met or converged
79:   # has no edge to take, and the Run ends where it stands.
80:   - { from: next-period, to: synthesize, revisit: true }

1: # opene902 timing probe
2: 
3: A HimaPack that answers one question about one design: **which tested clock periods satisfy setup timing, and what should be tried next?** It synthesizes `opene902` at a chosen period in a workspace of its
4: own, reads the qor report the run produced, judges it against the setup constraint and the goal, and
5: chooses the next period to try from what it measured — never from what it hoped. Then it goes round
6: again with that period, and keeps going until the goal is met, the periods stop moving, or the
7: Campaign's generation allowance is spent.
8: 
9: This is the first pack, and it is deliberately the smallest thing that is still a real Campaign: one
10: strategy knob, one tool, one report, two rules, one chooser, one loop. Everything a bigger pack will
11: need — more knobs, more reports, a drill-down loop inside this one — is the same parts with more in
12: each.
13: 
14: Method version **2** changes only the default chooser binding from the legacy `timing-push`
15: guard band to the existing `over-constraining-push` step. Graph and contract both declare version 2.
16: The reference graph topology, tools, reader and Judge rules remain unchanged.
17: 
18: ## What one generation does
19: 
20: 1. **`synthesize`** (act) runs `tools/synth.sh` on the Site: `make … synth` inside the Campaign's own
21:    copy of the flow, at the strategy's clock period, forced so no generation reuses another's
22:    netlist.
23: 2. **`read-qor`** (act) reads `flow/results/<design>/syn/report/qor.rpt` through the
24:    `dc-qor-report@1` reader, which turns it into typed values: setup WNS, setup TNS, the clock
25:    period the run actually used, hold WNS, and cell area.
26: 3. **`judge`** (judge) applies two rules to those values and writes a verdict for each.
27: 4. **`next-period`** (explore) runs the `over-constraining-push` chooser over the verdicts and the values and
28:    records the next strategy with its reasoning.
29: 
30: Then, if the decision was a next period, the Run follows the `revisit` edge from `next-period` back
31: to `synthesize` and does all four again as the next generation, at that period. A `blocked` wait node
32: is declared for the Hard blockers a node's spent Retry allowance produces; nothing draws an edge to
33: it, because the fabric routes a Run there itself.
34: 
35: ## The Campaign: generation after generation
36: 
37: A **generation** is one pass of those four nodes: one synthesis at one period, read, judged, decided.
38: The first is generation one, and every record it leaves — the node transitions, the Job, the
39: observation, the verdicts, the decision — says which generation it belongs to, so the ledger reads as
40: the exploration ran. The Retry allowance is per node *per generation*: a synthesis that failed twice
41: in generation two starts generation three's allowance afresh, because a retry under a new period is
42: not a third go at the old one.
43: 
44: A Campaign of this pack ends in one of four ways, and the run row says which:
45: 
46: - **`ended-goal-met`** — a generation closed its setup timing *and* reached the target period. The
47:   question is answered and no further licence-minute is spent on it.
48: - **`ended-converged`** — the exploration has stopped learning. `next-period` declares what that
49:   means, as data, in the chooser's own vocabulary:
50: 
51:   ```yaml
52:   converge:
53:     read: period        # one of the chooser's own reads
54:     band: 0.05          # ns: how far apart two generations' periods must be to count as movement
55:     generations: 1      # how many successive generations must have moved by less than that
56:     generationLimit: 6  # this pack's default allowance, which a person may override
57:   ```
58: 
59:   The 0.05 ns band is the exploration step. This ending states only that consecutive
60:   measured periods moved by less than that band. It does **not** prove the Goal was met,
61:   the last generation met setup, or a global optimum was found. A repeated violation may
62:   converge; use the recorded verdicts to distinguish it from a measured closed result.
63: 
64:   The decision record carries the whole rule — the read, the band, the generations counted, and the
65:   periods compared — so a person can re-derive the ending from one record, and `/hima status` and the
66:   workbench card say it in words.
67: - **`ended-budget-exhausted`** — a meter ran out. `generation-limit` is the Loop's own: the Campaign
68:   reached the generation it was allowed and the revisit that would have opened the next one did not
69:   happen, with the period it would have tried still on record. `time-box` is the other.
70: - **`waiting`** — a node spent its Retry allowance and the Run is at `blocked`, for a person.
71: 
72: The generation limit is a **Budget** meter and not a convergence: convergence is what the exploration
73: learned, the limit is what the Campaign was allowed to spend learning it. `converge.generationLimit`
74: above is this pack's default; `/hima run … --generations <n>` (and the same field on the start route)
75: overrides it, and what the Run is actually held to is on its Budget from the moment it opens.
76: 
77: The local Site generates **stand-in** reports, with `setup_wns = min(0, period − 2.20)` ns.
78: These are controlled test numbers, not measured Design Compiler or silicon improvements.
79: From 2.30 ns, method 2 gives the following bounded examples:
80: 
81: | Goal | Measured periods (ns) | Ending |
82: | --- | --- | --- |
83: | 2.25 ns | 2.30, 2.25 | goal met; the last generation passes both rules |
84: | 2.00 ns | 2.30, 2.25, 2.20, 2.15, 2.15 | converged; the last two generations violate setup and the Goal remains unmet |
85: | 2.00 ns, one generation allowed, starting at 2.00 | 2.00 | generation limit; no measured setup-PASS result exists |
86: 
87: For the converged example, the best **measured setup-PASS** period is 2.20 ns. The 2.15 ns
88: requested period is a violation, and `period + |slack|` is a hypothesis about a possible period,
89: not a new measurement. An unexecuted next Strategy must never be included among measured results.
90: If there is no completed setup-PASS observation, there is no measured closed result to report.
91: The report's generation rows, verdicts, observation IDs and raw qor/logs provide the evidence;
92: this Pack does not add a second best-result computation to the Harness.
93: 
94: ## The goal template
95: 
96: A Campaign binds one number when it starts:
97: 
98: ```
99: target_period_ns = <the clock period this design must close on, in ns>
100: ```
101: 
102: That number is bound into the goal rule `clock-period-at-most@1`, whose predicate is
103: `clock_period ≤ target_period_ns`. The rule file states the comparison; the Campaign states the
104: target. One rule therefore serves every target period, and the run cannot widen its own goal to
105: manufacture a pass — the bound value lands on the verdict, where a person can read what was actually
106: asked for.
107: 
108: `target_period_ns` is the name the harness carries it under; what a person reads is the words this
109: pack declares for it under `words:` in `contract.yml` — **clock period at most**, in **ns**. So a
110: card and `/hima status` say `goal: clock period at most 2.3 ns`, not `goal: target_period_ns=2.3`,
111: while every route still answers under the name. The number keeps whatever precision it was given: a
112: face shows what the ledger holds and rounds nothing. A pack that declares no words for a number shows
113: it under the name; this one declares both of its numbers, this and the strategy knob below.
114: 
115: The setup constraint is the same one step 1 checks, unparameterised:
116: `setup-wns-all-nonnegative@1`, `setup_wns ≥ 0` over all paths. A generation that closes its own
117: setup timing but misses the target is a real result, not a failure: it says the design closes, but
118: not yet where the goal is.
119: 
120: The judge applies the rules in the order `graph.yml` lists them, and the outgoing edge is chosen by
121: the outcome of the **first** — the setup rule. The goal rule decides whether the Campaign is done,
122: not which way the graph goes.
123: 
124: ## The strategy knob
125: 
126: One knob: **`periodNs`**, the clock period handed to `CLOCK_PERIOD_NS` for that generation. It is
127: the only thing that changes between generations of this pack. The flow accepts it as a command-line
128: variable, so nothing in the flow is edited to try a new value.
129: 
130: The knob is this pack's, declared in `contract.yml` under `strategy:` with everything about it in
131: one place — its type, its unit, its bounds and the value a campaign starts at:
132: 
133: ```yaml
134: strategy:
135:   periodNs: { type: number, unit: ns, min: 0.5, max: 10, default: 2.30 }
136: ```
137: 
138: The bounds are what a person could plausibly ask *this flow* for and not what this design closes at:
139: they hold every period this pack has been run at on the stand-in and on the reference site, and they
140: refuse a mistyped `0` or `100` before a campaign exists, in the same words at the window's start
141: form, at `--set periodNs=<ns>` and in a request body. The default is what the start form fills in
142: and what a run that sets nothing is started at.
143: 
144: Its words, declared beside the goal parameter's under `words:`, are **clock period** in **ns**: a
145: face says `strategy: clock period 2.25 ns`, and the run row and the routes go on carrying
146: `periodNs`.
147: 
148: The period a generation was judged on is read back from the report (`clock_period`), never assumed
149: from the number that was asked for. A tool that silently clamped the period, or a reused netlist from
150: an earlier run, would otherwise be judged as if it had honoured the request.
151: 
152: ## The chooser and its exploration step
153: 
154: `over-constraining-push` uses **stepNs = 0.05 ns**. Given the recorded setup verdict,
155: goal verdict, `clock_period` and `setup_wns`:
156: 
157: - **Both PASS**: end goal-met; do not propose another experiment.
158: - **Setup PASS, Goal not met**: try `clock_period − stepNs`. A met constraint does not
159:   need to expose positive slack for exploration to continue.
160: - **Setup FAIL**: try `clock_period + |setup_wns| − stepNs`. This is a proposed experiment,
161:   not evidence that the design closes at the inferred period.
162: 
163: Goal-met is checked first, then the Pack's convergence rule, then a next Strategy.
164: The chooser remains deterministic YAML in `choosers/over-constraining-push.yml`;
165: no model participates in this sample's strategy selection. The Ledger decision records its
166: inputs, parameters and cited verdicts/observation. Broader AI research belongs to the later Pack.
167: 
168: ### Why the default changed
169: 
170: The historical Step 3 reference-site trace reported zero setup slack at met constraints.
171: The old `timing-push` PASS clause therefore increased the requested period by 0.05 ns every
172: generation. On the calibrated stand-in, starting at 2.30 ns produces 2.30, 2.35, 2.40,
173: 2.45, 2.50, 2.55 and stops at the generation limit. That failure remains an explicitly
174: named `legacy-timing-push-probe` test variant; the old chooser file is retained unchanged.
175: 
176: Version 2 avoids relying on positive margin in that case. The local examples prove the
177: mechanism under their stated arithmetic, not a universal property of Design Compiler, all
178: designs or synthesis settings. Real Site efficacy requires a separate measured validation.
179: Historical records belong to their original method version and must not be relabeled as v2.
180: 
181: ## What a Site must bind
182: 
183: `contract.yml` names three inputs; a Site binds them in its own file under `bindings:`.
184: 
185: | Input | On `linglong` | On the local site |
186: | --- | --- | --- |
187: | `flowRoot` | `/data/eda/project/design_zoo` — the Site's Design Zoo | the generated stand-in flow |
188: | `design` | `opene902` | `opene902` |
189: | `workspaceRoot` | `/data/eda/project/hima_harness` | the isolated home's workspace |
190: 
191: Nothing else about the pack changes between the two. That is what the run contract is for:
192: `/hima pack check opene902-timing-probe --site <site>` says, before anything runs, whether a Site can
193: host this pack — every input bound, every tool's first word a wrapper the Permit allows, every rule
194: and reader resolvable, and every licence a tool holds declared by the Site in at least that number.
195: 
196: ## What a generation holds
197: 
198: `synth` holds **one `Design-Compiler` seat** for as long as its Job runs, declared on the tool in
199: `contract.yml`. A Site says how many seats it has under `capacity.licences` — `linglong` declares 99
200: — and the count is held across every Run of that Site, exactly as the parallel job cap is, because a
201: licence belongs to the Site and not to a Campaign. A launch that would take one seat too many waits
202: for one to come free, and says so on the node; a Site that declares fewer seats than this tool holds
203: (or none, which is what a node-locked tool's `0` means) cannot host the pack at all, and the check
204: says so rather than letting a Run wait for a seat that will never come free.
205: 
206: The other tool a person might expect here — Innovus — is not in this pack, which is why nothing
207: declares the reference site's `Innovus_Impl_System: 0`.
208: 
209: ## Where a generation runs
210: 
211: Never in `flowRoot`. `/hima pack prepare` copies the flow's makefile, its `flows/` and `manifests/`
212: directories, and the design's `build/` and `sources/` trees (about 56 MB for `opene902`) into
213: `<workspaceRoot>/<campaign>/flow/`, and every generation of that Campaign runs there. The flow
214: derives its project root from its own location, so the copy builds into the copy.
215: 
216: The one thing that does *not* follow from the copy's location is the container the flow's wrapper
217: runs in: it creates a container by name and binds the project root into it, so a copy run under the
218: Site's own container name would write the Site's own results after all. Hence
219: `EDA_CONTAINER_NAME=hima-<campaign>` on every tool line, and the container's name recorded in the
220: workspace's `workspace.json` so a later cleanup knows what to remove.
221: 
222: ## What the Campaign leaves for the next one
223: 
224: Every ended Run of this pack writes its own technical report into the Campaign workspace, beside the
225: results: `<workspaceRoot>/<campaign>/hima-experience/<runId>.md` for the people who read it and
226: `<runId>.json` for the programs that do. Nothing in this pack's three files asks for it — the harness
227: writes it for every pack, whatever ending the Run reached, a cancel and a spent time box included —
228: and it is written where the results are and left there, because the evidence of a Campaign belongs to
229: the Site owner and outlives the session that produced it. HimaLedger keeps only each file's path,
230: size and SHA-256, so a person who fetches one months later can hold it against what the Campaign
231: actually wrote.
232: 
233: What the Markdown holds is this pack's own story: the ending and why, the goal that was bound and
234: the Site it ran on, every Budget meter against its bound, one row per generation with the period it
235: asked for, the period and slack it measured, its verdicts and its decision, then a paragraph per
236: generation saying the same in sentences — *It asked the flow for 2.25 ns and measured 2.25 ns, with
237: 0.00 ns of setup slack. HimaJudge found PASS on setup-wns-all-nonnegative, FAIL on
238: clock-period-at-most. The decision was …* — and finally the path the Run took, any Hard blockers,
239: and any cancel. So the file answers, without the ledger, the two questions a pack author is asked
240: about a Campaign that has finished: what did it learn, and why did it stop.
241: 
242: A person reads it in three places without going to the Site: the card's evidence drawer on an ended
243: Run, the `.md` route the drawer links to, and `/hima status <run>`, which names both paths.

(End of file - total 243 lines)
</content>

<content>
1: #!/bin/sh
2: # The `synth` tool of the opene902 timing probe: one synthesis generation at a chosen clock period.
3: #
4: # The command line below is the one `contract.yml` declares for this tool, so a person can reproduce
5: # a generation by hand exactly as HimaFabric runs it:
6: #
7: #   WORKSPACE=/data/eda/project/hima_harness/<campaign> \
8: #   FLOW_ROOT=/data/eda/project/design_zoo \
9: #   DESIGN=opene902 PERIOD_NS=2.20 CAMPAIGN=<campaign> \
10: #   sh packs/opene902-timing-probe/tools/synth.sh
11: #
12: # Three things about that line are the whole point of it:
13: #   - `-C "$WORKSPACE/flow"` runs the Campaign's own copy of the flow. The flow derives its project
14: #     root from its own location, so the copy builds into the copy and the Site's own results under
15: #     $FLOW_ROOT are never written.
16: #   - `FORCE_SYNTH=1` because the flow reuses an existing netlist otherwise, and a generation that
17: #     reused the previous one's netlist would be judged on a period it never ran at.
18: #   - `EDA_CONTAINER_NAME=hima-$CAMPAIGN` because the flow's wrapper CREATES a container of that name
19: #     on first use and binds $PROJECT_ROOT into it. Running the copy under the Site's own container
20: #     name would bind the Site's flow instead and write the Site's results (D19).
21: set -eu
22: 
23: : "${WORKSPACE:?the Campaign workspace on the Site}"
24: : "${FLOW_ROOT:?the Site's flow root, for the record: the generation runs in the workspace copy}"
25: : "${DESIGN:?the design to synthesize}"

1: # The chooser of a timing push that knows its business: it over-constrains on purpose and reads the
2: # violation the tool answers with. Data, never code (D38), beside `timing-push.yml`, for a pack whose
3: # knob is a clock period judged against a setup constraint.
4: #
5: # Why a second push rule exists at all (D45). `timing-push` asks a met period how much margin it had
6: # and pushes by the answer. A tool that reports no margin for a met period does not answer that
7: # question: it states a setup slack of exactly 0.00 whenever the period it was given is met, because
8: # it stops optimizing the moment the constraint is satisfied. So on such a tool that clause reads
9: # `period − 0 + guardBand` and loosens the period by the guard band every generation, which is the
10: # trace the step-3 acceptance on the reference site recorded (D45) — six generations walking from
11: # 2.28 ns out to 2.53 ns, converging on nothing.
12: #
13: # The method here never asks a met period what it had to spare. It asks for less than it believes is
14: # possible and lets the tool say by how much it was wrong:
15: #
16: # - The constraint PASSED — the tool said nothing about the margin, because a met period is all it
17: #   says. Take one step tighter and ask again; that is the over-constraining, and `stepNs` is how
18: #   coarse the walk in is.
19: # - The constraint FAILED — now the tool has stated something: the design missed by `|slack|`, so
20: #   `period + |slack|` is the period it can actually close at. Ask for one step less than that. The
21: #   next generation misses by that same step, states the same achievable period, and asks for the
22: #   same number again — two successive generations asking and measuring the same period, which is
23: #   what a pack's `converge:` calls having stopped learning. The violation is on record, which is
24: #   the fact the Campaign was run to find.
25: # - Both the constraint and the goal PASSED — the design closed and reached what the Run was for.
26: #   There is no next strategy; the decision is that the Goal is met.
27: #
28: # So a Campaign on this chooser ends `ended-goal-met` when the goal is reachable and
29: # `ended-converged` one step below the achievable period when it is not, on a tool that reports zero
30: # slack for a met period and on one that reports a real margin alike: the PASS clause never reads the
31: # margin, so it cannot be misled by a tool that has none to give.
32: id: over-constraining-push
33: version: '1'
34: title: Over-constrain the clock period by one step and read the violation
35: 
36: # The one number a pack binds, in its explore node's `bind:`: how far the walk in moves each
37: # generation while nothing is violated, and how far above the violated period the exploration settles.
38: parameter:
39:   name: stepNs
40:   unit: ns
41: 
42: # What is read out of the Run's latest observation, exactly as `timing-push` reads it: the period is
43: # the one the report stated and never the one the Run asked for, so a tool that clamped the period is
44: # not pushed against as if it had honoured the request.
45: reads:
46:   period: { type: clock_period, unit: ns }
47:   slack: { type: setup_wns, unit: ns }
48: 
49: # First matching `when` wins. `constraint` is the verdict of the judge node's first rule — the one
50: # the outgoing edge was chosen by — and `goal` the verdict of its goal rule.
51: # `next` sets the pack's own strategy knobs by name, and a knob it does not name carries over. This
52: # chooser is for a pack whose knob is a clock period; the name below is the one such a contract
53: # declares it under, and `/hima pack check` holds the two against each other before a campaign runs.
54: decide:
55:   - when: { constraint: PASS, goal: PASS }
56:     goalMet: true
57:   - when: { constraint: PASS }
58:     next:
59:       periodNs: { sum: [period, { neg: stepNs }] }
60:   - when: { constraint: FAIL }
61:     next:
62:       periodNs: { sum: [period, { abs: slack }, { neg: stepNs }] }

(End of file - total 62 lines)
</content>

10: # declared, the unit the declared one, `mode` and `scope` carried exactly where they are declared.

12: # analysis pass over one path group and a number that forgot which is a number nobody can compare.

<content>
1: ## Goal template
2: 
3: The primary target: **the measured sum reaches the goal minimum.**
4: 
5: - Parameter `minimum` — unit **count**, bounds 0..10000, default 1. This test Run explicitly requests `minimum=1`. What it means: the acceptance bound that the measured sum must reach. It is a bound and nothing else — never the number to fabricate, and never the output.
6: - The value the Goal is judged on is `numeric_sum` (unit count), the sum of the actual measured values strictly greater than LIMIT, read from the declared measured output `result.txt`.
7: 
8: Shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`: the target is stated as a value a reader actually produces rather than as a description of a mood, so the ending it declares can be detected by a number.
9: 
10: ## Constraints
11: 
12: Every constraint the Goal carries, typed and checkable, with the options the measurement was made under. Shaped by `assert-the-checker-options.md`: the options below are declared and asserted rather than inferred from the result — a sum whose options were not asserted is a number whose meaning nobody can state afterwards.
13: 
14: - **C1 — the strict-greater rule (count).** Only actual measured values strictly greater than LIMIT are summed, and equality to LIMIT is excluded. Checkable: the reading is valid only alongside the LIMIT of its Run, which the Workshop receives as `${LIMIT}` bound from the strategy scalar `limit` (unit count, bounds 0..100, default 18).
15: - **C2 — the input shape.** One nonnegative integer per line, in the flow's `numbers.txt`, carried into the campaign workspace's private flow copy. Checkable at preparation: the flow's own `prepare.sh` copies it to `measured.txt` unchanged, so the measured data is a byte copy and no transformation is implied.
16: - **C3 — the integer alone.** `result.txt` holds the integer sum alone, with no decoration. Checkable: anything else is a hard blocker — never a zero sum, and never a conclusion.
17: - **C4 — the options the measurement was made under, declared as a list.** Source: the declared measured output `measured.txt` in the campaign's private flow copy, and nothing else. Boundary: strictly greater than LIMIT. Unit: count. No EDA. No licence. These are asserted beside the reading, not reconstructed from it.
18: - **C5 — the bound is not the output.** The goal `minimum` is the acceptance bound; the output is the measured sum. Checkable: what is read is `numeric_sum`, never `minimum`.
19: 
20: `attribute-by-database-relation.md` shapes nothing in this section: this business has no database, no EDA, no licence and no adoption relation to query, so no relation-shaped constraint is authored.
21: 
22: ## Run contract
23: 
24: What a Site must bind, and what it must allow, for this pack to run at all.
25: 
26: **Inputs a Site must bind**
27: - The Golden Flow's data and preparation script: `numbers.txt` and `prepare.sh`, carried as-is into the campaign workspace's private flow copy at `${WORKSPACE}/flow/`. The reference flow stays where it lies, read-only, and is never written.
28: - The goal parameter `minimum` (unit count, bounds 0..10000, default 1).
29: - The strategy scalar `limit` (unit count, bounds 0..100, default 18), bound to the Workshop's `${LIMIT}`.
30: - One generation: this method has no chooser and no revisit, so the Campaign opens no second generation.
31: 
32: **Outputs**
33: - `${WORKSPACE}/flow/measured.txt` — the prepared measured data.
34: - `${WORKSPACE}/result.txt` — the integer sum alone.
35: - The reading `numeric_sum`.
36: 
37: **Tools, each with the wrapper this section declares for it**
38: - **preparation** — wrapper `sh prepare.sh <flow-directory>`, run against the private copy `${WORKSPACE}/flow`, writing `${WORKSPACE}/flow/measured.txt`. Its inputs are the flow's `numbers.txt` and `prepare.sh`, which the workspace copy carries, so no earlier tool of this pack has to produce them.
39: - **Workshop** — wrapper `sh ${ENTRY} ${WORKSPACE} ${LIMIT}`, the real act node: `$1` is the workspace and `$2` is the LIMIT. The script the Workshop generates is run with that same workspace as its own `$1`, so its `$1/flow/measured.txt` is the prepared measured data and its `$1/result.txt` is the integer alone.
40: - **observation** — wrapper: the declared custom reader over `${WORKSPACE}/result.txt`, producing `numeric_sum` in count. It reads nothing else.
41: - **the hard-blocker wait** — the node a Campaign stops at for a person; reached by the FAIL of judge rule R1, and equally when the declared measured output never reads as the integer alone.
42: - The Site must allow a shell (`sh`), a file copy, and writes inside the campaign's own private workspace only — which is where `${WORKSPACE}/flow/`, the private research directory `${WORKSPACE}/research/` and `${WORKSPACE}/result.txt` all live.
43: 
44: Shaped by `what-a-golden-flow-is.md`: the flow is reference material and never the goal, so the contract binds the flow's own stage by pointer and lets the campaign's workspace preparation make the copy it names; this pack copies no file of the flow into itself.
45: 
46: ## Semantics
47: 
48: One entry, and it is the only value any reader of this pack produces.
49: 
50: - `numeric_sum` — unit **count**. What it measures: the sum of the actual measured values strictly greater than LIMIT, read as the integer alone from the declared measured output `result.txt`. It is the output itself, not an estimate of one.
51: 
52: The goal `minimum` (declared in Goal template) and the strategy `limit` (declared in Run contract) are parameters this pack is given, not values any reader produces, which is why neither is declared here.
53: 
54: Shaped by `assert-the-checker-options.md`: the single value carries its unit and is a fact only alongside the LIMIT of its Run, so no reader can infer the rule deck from the number. `one-checker-per-session.md` bears on no further value here: this business runs exactly one analysis tool in one session, so there is no second count to split and none to sum across.
55: 
56: ## Judge rules
57: 
58: - **R1 — the goal rule, `numeric_sum >= minimum`.** Reads the declared value `numeric_sum` (unit count) and the goal parameter `minimum` (Goal template, unit count).
59:   - **PASS** → the Campaign's goal is met: the ending `goal-met`. The verdict cites `numeric_sum`, the `minimum` of the Run, and the LIMIT the sum was computed under.
60:   - **FAIL** (`numeric_sum < minimum`) → the hard-blocker wait node, and the ending `blocked`. The verdict cites `numeric_sum`, the `minimum` of the Run and the LIMIT of the Run. This is a fact about an analysis that did not reach its bound, and never a successful analysis.
61:   - **No value at all** — the declared measured output could not be read as the integer alone — routes to the hard-blocker wait node as well: no verdict is possible, and an unreadable result is a blocker rather than a zero.
62: 
63: Shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`: every outcome of the rule routes to an ending this pack declares, and the rule names the value that detects it.
64: 
65: ## Choosers
66: 
67: This pack declares **no chooser**, and it must not gain one. The method is one generation with no revisit, so there is no move to choose and no next target to set. `goal-met` is therefore reached by the PASS of the goal judge rule R1 itself, which ends the Campaign without a chooser clause; and there is no converge block to declare, because no value is watched across generations.
68: 
69: No knowledge file shaped this section. `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md` would add one — a chooser that reads a violation and sets a corrected or tighter next target — and the author has not asked for it: this method never revisits, so a chooser would be a stage the business does not have.
70: 
71: ## Endings
72: 
73: - **`goal-met`** — reached by the PASS of judge rule R1: `numeric_sum >= minimum`. Stated with the reading, the `minimum` of the Run, and the LIMIT the sum was computed under.
74: - **`blocked`** — reached by the FAIL of judge rule R1 (`numeric_sum < minimum`) routing to the hard-blocker wait node, and equally when the declared measured output never reads as the integer alone, so no `numeric_sum` exists to judge. A fact, stopped for a person, and never dressed up as a successful analysis.
75: - **budget-exhausted** — reached by the Campaign's generation allowance being spent. It is a budget and not a conclusion: it protects the Site and the person's time, and when it is reached the report says so plainly instead of calling it an analysis.
76: - `converged` is **not** an ending of this pack, and is not listed as one: with one generation and no chooser there is no value watched across generations, so nothing can be observed to stop changing. It is declared unavailable by construction rather than left implicit.
77: 
78: Shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`: every ending above is one a rule's outcome or a budget actually reaches, and the generation limit stays a budget rather than being dressed up as a result.
79: 
80: ## Workshops
81: 
82: - **Purpose.** At run time the Workshop authors its own shell script: the analysis of this Run. Nothing of that script is written at method-authoring time.
83: - **Inputs it is given.** `sh ${ENTRY} ${WORKSPACE} ${LIMIT}` — the workspace as `$1`, the LIMIT as `$2`. It reads the prepared measured data at `${WORKSPACE}/flow/measured.txt`, and it is written from the pack's declared knowledge file `knowledge/numeric-sum.md`, which explains the exact sum.
84: - **What it must produce, and the semantics of it.** `${WORKSPACE}/result.txt`, holding the integer sum alone: the reading `numeric_sum` in unit count, the sum of the actual measured values strictly greater than LIMIT with equality excluded. That is the value `Semantics` declares.
85: - **Where the generated code lives.** In the private research directory `${WORKSPACE}/research/`, inside the campaign's own workspace — never in this pack folder and never in the reference flow.
86:

**`tools/read-numeric-sum.sh`**

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# The reader of authored-numeric's judged output, launched through `readers/numeric-sum-file.yml` as:
#
#   sh tools/read-numeric-sum.sh <report> <out>
#
# $1 is the Workshop's result file and $2 is the reading document this script must write. The result
# file holds the integer sum alone — one line, digits, nothing around it.
#
# A file holding anything else is not a reading of this method: an empty file, a decimal, a sign, a
# second line, decoration around the number. The document then carries `"value": null` with the
# reason, so HimaJudge has no number to rule on and the Run stops at the wait node for a person. A
# zero is never written in place of a number nobody read.
set -eu

: "${1:?the result file to read}"
: "${2:?the reading document to write}"

report=$1
out=$2

if [ ! -f "$report" ]; then
  printf 'result file does not exist: %s\n' "$report" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# The integer sum alone: exactly one line, and that line all digits.
value=$(awk 'END { if (NR == 1 && $0 ~ /^[0-9]+$/) { print $0 } else { exit 1 } }' "$report") || value=

# A whole-file read leaves the digits as the Workshop spelled them; drop any leading zeros so the
# number the document states is a plain decimal. `0` itself stays `0`.
if [ -n "$value" ]; then
  value=$(printf '%s' "$value" | sed 's/^0*//')
  [ -n "$value" ] || value=0
  printf '{"values":[{"type":"numeric_sum","unit":"count","value":%s}]}\n' "$value" > "$out"
else
  printf '{"values":[{"type":"numeric_sum","unit":"count","value":null,"unknownReason":"the result file does not hold the integer sum alone"}]}\n' > "$out"
fi
```

**Review tools/read-numeric-sum.sh: reads the Workshop's result.txt and writes the numeric_sum reading document, emitting `"value": null` with a reason when the file does not hold the integer alone — approve, or say what to change**
